Coordinator snapshot archive, isolated (no other batch task ran
concurrently). Commits the Executor's claim-class audit tool, its test
suite, five regression fixtures, and the superseding knowledge entry
together with their own receipt in one commit, per the lesson from
TASK-20260809-c30f26: a receipt's path_sha256/commit_sha must be
verifiable from a single commit's diff, not reconstructed after the
fact across two.

Independent verification performed before archiving (see receipt):
- All 5 fixtures re-parsed via yaml.safe_load; each matches its
  specified evasion shape (nested/multiline/quoted flow, block
  trailing comment, block quoted).
- Both pre-v2 regex audits (AUDIT-1/AUDIT-2 in
  knowledge/TAG-CLAIM-CLASS.md) re-run against the fixtures; neither
  catches any of the 5 -- confirmed genuine evasions, not contrived.
- knowledge/TAG-CLAIM-CLASS.md confirmed byte-for-byte unedited
  (git diff --exit-code); TAG-CLAIM-CLASS-v2.md supersedes it via a
  new file, per R-CC-6.
- GATE-A case G11 (tags as YAML !!set) reconstructed from scratch and
  re-run against tools/claim_class_audit.py; the set/frozenset branch
  is load-bearing, not decorative.
- tools/test_claim_class_audit.py: 27/27 pass.
- tools/validate_ledger.py: OK, 5564 records, zero new violations.

  independently reproduced as already-retired via supersedes:.

to TASK-20260809-c30f26 earlier in this batch.

The reviewer's substance holds: an independent B4-form evasion probe,
built from validation_report.yaml's specification rather than copied
from the Executor's fixture, confirmed genuine and caught; byte-identity
of knowledge/TAG-CLAIM-CLASS.md re-derived via sha256 at three commits
plus the working tree; the fixtures confirmed outside knowledge/;
TAG-CLAIM-CLASS-v2.md's supersession of AUDIT-1/AUDIT-2 confirmed
additive-only via a programmatic rule-by-rule diff, its one non-additive
change (dropping supersession-awareness) disclosed and its stated
four-hit consequence reproduced exactly against the real corpus.

Independently re-verified before archiving, not taken on the reviewer's
word (full list in this task's own receipt): the B4 probe was rebuilt
from scratch in a throwaway location and re-run against both legacy
audits and the new script, same result; the dangling "execution report"
citations were confirmed real via grep, and a repository-wide search
confirmed no execution_report artifact exists for TASK-20260809-3e30b8
specifically; TAG-CLAIM-CLASS.md's single-commit history and
byte-identity were independently re-run.

The review named two required fixes for full PASS: (a) archive a real
execution_report for TASK-20260809-3e30b8, or correct the dangling
citations to point at what is actually committed; (b) a stale
dispatch_queue.json state for TASK-20260809-3e30b8, corrected in the
next commit alongside this one's own state/hash backfill. Per the
handoff's instruction, (a) is recorded as the batch's next_action
rather than performed here -- it requires either reconstructing a
genuine break-attempt log or editing the Executor's own committed code,
neither of which is this archive task's declared scope.

This commit changes exactly TASK-20260809-c8122d's declared archive
scope (the receipt and the review report) and nothing else -- the
dispatch_queue.json state updates ride the following commit, per the
lesson already learned twice this session about keeping an archive
commit's diff exactly equal to its declared expected_paths.
